Pull request description:

  This PR marks the `bitcoin-build-config.h` header with the dedicated [`IWYU pragma: always_keep`](https://github.com/include-what-you-use/include-what-you-use/blob/master/docs/IWYUPragmas.md#iwyu-pragma-always_keep), which makes the per-include `IWYU pragma: keep` comments redundant.

  As a result, grepping for `IWYU pragma: keep` returns only the genuine use cases, each of which should be properly documented.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36451: refactor: Use NotNull for CreateNewBlock and pimpls

fa9158641839e6dbc3cab63b07929998247b1f97 refactor: Return NotNull from CreateNewBlock (MarcoFalke)
fa071a2c451d2cab12e181711b2dd64d61f3ea18 refactor: Mark pimpls as NotNull (MarcoFalke)
fa4785828e804f44726102070fb1adeacbdce6e5 util: refactor: Add and use MakeNotNullShared and MakeNotNullUnique (MarcoFalke)
faf85b0321797a811260a90f6b9a839a9ad9e3c2 test: Add some NotNull test cases (MarcoFalke)

Pull request description:

  Current code uses nullable smart pointers for some stuff that is never null. This is perfectly fine, but a bit confusing:

  * When reading the code, it is not clear which pointer is nullable or never null.
  * Pointers that are never null still have confusing null checks (with possible error handling return branches), which are always dead in coverage reports or when applying mutation testing.
  * While some places have the redundant null checks on pointers that are never null, other places do not, which adds to the confusion.

  Clarify this at compile-time by using `NotNull` (or a plain reference)

commit.message:
scripted-diff: Drop `IWYU pragma: keep` from build config includes

The `bitcoin-build-config.h` header is now marked with
`IWYU pragma: always_keep`, which makes the per-include
`IWYU pragma: keep` comments redundant.

-BEGIN VERIFY SCRIPT-
OLD='#include <bitcoin-build-config.h> // IWYU pragma: keep'
NEW='#include <bitcoin-build-config.h>'
sed -i "s|$OLD|$NEW|" $(git grep -l "$OLD")

GUARD='#ifndef BITCOIN_CONFIG_H'
PRAGMA='// IWYU pragma: always_keep'
sed -i "s|^$GUARD$|$PRAGMA\n\n&|" cmake/bitcoin-build-config.h.in
-END VERIFY SCRIPT-

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36862: test: use long timeout for event waits in interface_ipc_mining

74135e2e625030b18daf7539bd19dabb75948af1 test: use long timeout for event waits in interface_ipc_mining (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  Follow-up to #36791, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36791#discussion_r4565761925 by ryanofsky.

  #36791 fixed the `waitTipChanged` timeout on slow hosts, but the `template6` `waitNext` call has the same race: it waits for an event the test triggers after a 0.1s sleep, with a 1s timeout.

  This adds `long_ipc_timeout` and uses it for all waits that end on an event the test triggers.

  To reproduce failure on master:

  ```diff
  diff --git a/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py b/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
  index cdef196fd0..49e1c8a9c1 100755
  --- a/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
  +++ b/test/functional/interface_ipc_mining.py
  @@ -320,7 +320,8 @@ class IPCMiningTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
                   self.log.debug("Wait for another, get one after increase in fees in the mempool")
                   template6 = await wait_and_do(
                       mining_wait_next_template(template5, stack, ctx, waitoptions),
  -                    lambda: self.miniwallet.send_self_transfer(fee_rate=10, from_node=self.nodes[0]))
  +                    lambda: self.miniwallet.send_self_transfer(fee_rate=10, from_node=self.nodes[0]),
  +                    sleep_time=1.2)
                   assert template6 is not None
                   block4 = await mining_get_block(template6, ctx)
                   assert_equal(len(block4.vtx), 3)

  ```

ACKs for top commit:
  nervana21:
    tACK 74135e2e625030b18daf7539bd19dabb75948af1
  ryanofsky:
    Tested ACK 74135e2e625030b18daf7539bd19dabb75948af1. This finishes the fix from #36791: every wait that returns on an event the test triggers now has at least a minute, so none of them can time out on a slow host with the default timeout factor. I checked that the test passes normally, with the faketime command from #36791, and with `sleep_time=1.2` on the `template6` wait, which failed before.

commit.message:
memusage: Make fields of STL helper structs public

The `stl_tree_node`, `list_node` and `unordered_node` class templates
only mimic the layout of the standard library's container nodes, so
that `sizeof` yields an estimate of the memory they use. Their fields
are never accessed.

Since llvm/llvm-project#237374, Clang 24 diagnoses these fields with
`-Wunused-private-field`.

This change drops the `private:` access specifiers. It does not affect
the size or alignment of the structs, as all their fields keep the same
access control, and it is consistent with `stl_shared_counter`.

  I raise the allowance to 3 bytes, which makes the failure about 200 times rarer. The check that the fee is not too low is unchanged. maflcko suggested 3 bytes in #24151 and #25164.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36757: net: ignore privacy network peer's view of our address

9cfd6014005197d9d2d67dacb3c079980e3b284c test: check privacy-network peers' view of our address is not used (stratospher)
533fee6b9da3801612f245af461fb2d8fb06f197 net: ignore privacy-network peers' view of our address (stratospher)

Pull request description:

  privacy networks set `addrMe` ("IP address peer thinks I am") in the VERSION message [as all zeroes](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/f103de70de0662a1395dca2e536cf5872d86eaa2/src/net_processing.cpp#L1667).
  this PR ensures we ignore it when processing VERSION message.

  this fixes a fingerprint which makes it possible to correlate clearnet and privacy network IPs but it requires some not so easy preconditions:
  1. we need to choose this adversarial tor/i2p peer to make an outbound connection to from our addrman
  2. we need to be using a unique enough port. this would become easier in a future if we ever support random ports.

  h/t to Loupe and instagibbs for finding this fingerprint!
